text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ailing Zimbabwe iron and steel company, Ziscosteel could see its viability restored as South Africa's third largest mining house, JCI, and US hydrocarbons company , Atlantic Richfield, team up to establish a reduced iron plant in Mozambique's Manica province. The plant would produce US$2.8 million tonnes per year of Zimbabwean iron ore.

- A report by the British Overseas Development Administration has shown that international donors are likely not to fund the compulsory acquisition of land under Zimbabwe's land redistribution scheme.
- Eight heads of state and government have confirmed that they will attend the sixth annual summit of the Group of 15 developing countries which starts in the Zimbabwe capital Harare on Sunday.

- Delivery of health services at Zimbabwe's major hospitals remained low on Friday with junior doctors milling about in corridors as little could be done without nurses, still on strike to press for salary hikes and improved working conditions.
- Zimbabwe's Agricultural Finance Corporation has budgeted more than Z$600 million for the financing of loans to the country's commercial farming sector during the 1996/97 agricultural season.
